solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Old storage media vs. opening corrupt files (8)

indicators.note: OPP opens the anagrammed word, sitting inside it

blocks.note: FILES rearranged, split FL…IES around the insert
vs. (versus) = opposed to, abbreviated opp.

annotation.surface: A complaint that old disks garble whatever files you open from them.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Opening' looks like part of the computer picture, but it tells OPP to go into the rearranged FILES, like a hole opening it up.
annotation.definitionFit: Floppies are floppy disks, the removable storage of 1980s and 90s computers.

entries.clue: Dog has a filling drink thus (5,4)

indicators.note: HAS A fills LAP, sitting inside it

blocks.note: to lap = to drink, as a dog does
taken as written, placed inside LAP
so = thus

annotation.surface: A dog enjoying a satisfying drink.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Has a' looks like grammar joining dog to drink, but it is literal letters dropped inside LAP.
annotation.definitionFit: The Lhasa apso is a small long-haired Tibetan breed of dog.

entries.clue: Left note to be received by long-ago reader (7)

indicators.note: L and MI are taken in by PAST, going inside it

blocks.note: long ago = past, opened up as PA…ST
L = left
mi, the third note of the sol-fa scale

annotation.surface: Someone leaves a note for a reader from long ago.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Reader' suggests books; here it is someone who reads palms.
annotation.definitionFit: A palmist reads the lines of people's hands to tell fortunes.

entries.clue: Local church possessed by erstwhile purity (9)

indicators.note: to be possessed by something is to be held by it, so CE is held inside ONCE

blocks.note: a local is a pub, here an inn
erstwhile = once, split O…NCE around the church
CE = Church of England

annotation.surface: Lost innocence of a village pub and church, gone for good.
annotation.walkthrough: In Britain a 'local' is the pub you drink at regularly, so it gives INN.
annotation.definitionFit: Innocence is purity, freedom from guilt or corruption.

entries.clue: Just one hand’s on nose (8,7)

blocks.note: a straight is a poker hand, plus the 's
hooter is British slang for the nose

annotation.surface: Someone has only one hand resting on their nose.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Just one' reads as 'only one' but means a just person. The word break moves: STRAIGHT'S + HOOTER becomes STRAIGHT SHOOTER.
annotation.definitionFit: A straight shooter is an honest, fair-dealing person: a just one.

entries.clue: Young lion is first for this painter (6)

blocks.note: a young lion is a cub
taken as written
first letter of 'this'

annotation.surface: A painter who puts a lion cub before everything else.
annotation.walkthrough: 'First' looks like 'foremost' in the surface, but it takes only the T of 'this'.
annotation.definitionFit: A Cubist is a painter in the style of Picasso and Braque.

entries.clue: Class project on Spain (5)

blocks.note: to cast = to project, as a shadow or light
E is Spain's international vehicle code

annotation.surface: A school class doing a project on Spain.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Project' reads as a school assignment, but it is the verb, to throw or cast.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a caste is a social class fixed by birth, as in the traditional Hindu system.

entries.clue: Steady job Alan certainly keeps (7)

indicators.note: the phrase holds the answer within it

blocks.note: the letters run across the word breaks, from the last letter of 'job' to two letters into 'certainly'

annotation.surface: Alan is certain to stay in his secure job.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Steady job' looks like one phrase; the definition is 'Steady' alone, and 'job' starts the hiding place.
annotation.definitionFit: A verb synonym: you balance a wobbly load, or steady it, by keeping it from tipping.

entries.clue: Medicinal plant, reddish brown, one’s taken out (5)

indicators.note: one, as the Roman numeral I, is taken out of the word, as a player is taken out of a side

blocks.note: sienna is a reddish-brown pigment

annotation.surface: A reddish-brown herb whose leaves have been plucked out.
annotation.walkthrough: I is the Roman numeral one.
annotation.definitionFit: Senna is a plant whose pods are used as a laxative.

entries.clue: In which fighters may get whacked? (3-2,9)

definitions.text: In which fighters may get whacked?

blocks.note: read as any combat sport, and meant as one particular freestyle kind of wrestling
read as 'may get hit', and meant as 'may get whacked' in the British sense of exhausted, which is 'all in'

annotation.surface: A question about a sport where fighters take a beating.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Whacked' reads as 'struck', but in British slang it also means exhausted, which is 'all in'.
annotation.definitionFit: All-in wrestling is freestyle wrestling with few rules, where fighters certainly get whacked.

entries.clue: Lump one found in bed? (4)

blocks.note: a small compressed mass, as of banknotes or chewing gum
I = one, the Roman numeral

annotation.surface: Something lumpy discovered in your bed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bed' suggests sleep; here it is a river bed.
annotation.definitionFit: A wadi is a dry river bed in the Middle East or North Africa.

entries.clue: Atrocity met by Sadat in old conflict (7,3)

blocks.note: an atrocity is a crime
Anwar Sadat, president of Egypt 1970-81

annotation.surface: Egypt's President Sadat confronting an atrocity in a past war.
annotation.walkthrough: The Egyptian president is known by his full name, Anwar Sadat; only the first name is used, and the letters then re-split across a new word break.
annotation.definitionFit: By example: this 1853-56 war of Russia against Britain, France and Turkey is one old conflict among many.

entries.clue: Precise time to open 23 (4,2)

indicators.note: T opens SPOON up by going inside it

blocks.note: 23 across is CLUB; a spoon is an old golf club
T = time

annotation.surface: An exact moment at which to open something.
annotation.walkthrough: The cross-reference points at the answer to 23 across, CLUB, and a spoon is one kind of golf club.
annotation.definitionFit: Spot on means exactly right, precise.

entries.clue: Criminal had a nice estate (8)

indicators.note: the letters are crooked, out of order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters

annotation.surface: A crook who owned a lovely country estate.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' looks like the subject of the sentence; it is only the instruction to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: A hacienda is a large estate in Spain or Latin America.

entries.clue: Humiliated, Charlie went with expedition (9)

blocks.note: Charlie is C in the NATO alphabet
expedition here means speed: went with speed, hurried

annotation.surface: Charlie comes back humbled from a journey.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Expedition' suggests a journey, but it also means promptness, so going with expedition is hastening.
annotation.definitionFit: To be chastened is to be humbled or subdued by a rebuke.

entries.clue: Irish county short of land for diggers? (4,5)

blocks.note: County Down, in Northern Ireland
under = short of, as in under par

annotation.surface: An Irish county lacking room for people who dig.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Diggers' is old slang for Australian soldiers, and Australians generally; Down Under is Australia.
annotation.definitionFit: By regional slang: a digger is an Australian soldier or, loosely, any Australian, and Down Under is the nickname for Australia.

entries.clue: See game that has knight in monster’s lair? (4,4)

indicators.note: a game that 'has' a knight in it holds that piece, so CHESS contains N

blocks.note: lo = see!, as in 'lo and behold'
split CH…ESS around the knight
N is the chess notation for a knight

annotation.surface: A chess game with a knight venturing into a dragon's den.
annotation.walkthrough: The knight looks like a fairy-tale hero at a monster's lair; it is just the chess symbol N, in a game of chess.
annotation.definitionFit: Loch Ness in Scotland is the supposed home of the Loch Ness Monster.

entries.clue: My talking, entirely to intimidate (4,3)

indicators.note: we want the sound of the word when spoken

blocks.note: entirely = wholly, which is said like HOLY
to cow = to intimidate

annotation.surface: Someone boasting that their speech is all about bullying people.
annotation.walkthrough: 'My' looks like a possessive, but it is the exclamation 'My!', as in surprise.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Holy cow!' and 'My!' are both cries of surprise.

entries.clue: Channel that’s not introduced local game (6)

indicators.note: drop the letter that introduces the word

blocks.note: a narrows is a narrow channel of water

annotation.surface: A TV channel that has not yet launched a regional sport.
annotation.walkthrough: A 'local' is a British pub, and arrows is pub slang for darts, the local game.
annotation.definitionFit: Arrows is a colloquial name for darts, a game played in the local pub.

entries.clue: Reading — next up, penning chapter one (7)

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read from the bottom
RETAL pens, encloses, C and I

blocks.note: next = later
C = chapter
I = one

annotation.surface: A reader announcing that chapter one comes up next.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Chapter one' looks like a single book reference; it is two separate abbreviations, C and I.
annotation.definitionFit: A recital is a reading aloud or recitation before an audience.

entries.clue: Dire Straits for lovers of the classics (10)

definitions.text: Dire Straits for lovers of the classics

blocks.note: read as the British rock band, and meant as a stretch of sea that proved disastrous
read as fans of classical music, and meant as the lovers of Greek myth, Hero and Leander, who drowned swimming to her

annotation.surface: Dire Straits, the band, recommended for fans of classic music.
annotation.walkthrough: The capitals point at the rock band, but these are real straits, disastrous for the classical lovers Hero and Leander.
annotation.definitionFit: The Hellespont (the Dardanelles) is the strait where, in Greek myth, Leander drowned swimming to Hero.

entries.clue: What frames pictures in our home? (5)

indicators.note: EH surrounds ART like a frame

blocks.note: 'Eh?' = 'What?'
pictures are art

annotation.surface: Asking what hangs the pictures in our house.
annotation.walkthrough: 'What' looks like the start of a question; it is EH, the questioning noise.
annotation.definitionFit: By description: the planet is home to all of us, so 'our home' paraphrases it.

entries.clue: Was bather quiet in flood? (5)

blocks.note: a bather swims, so 'was bather' = swam
p = piano, quiet in music

annotation.surface: Asking whether a swimmer stayed calm during a flood.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flood' is a verb here: to swamp something is to flood it.
annotation.definitionFit: A verb synonym: water that swamps a field floods it, filling it beyond capacity.

entries.clue: Order staff to strike (4)

blocks.note: an order is a society, like a religious or chivalric order
a staff is a stout stick used as a weapon
a third definition: the verb, to hit with a heavy stick

annotation.surface: An instruction for employees to go on strike.
annotation.walkthrough: This is really a triple definition: order, staff and to strike all mean CLUB. The surface reads as a union calling a walkout.
annotation.definitionFit: A club is a society, a heavy stick, and, as a verb, to hit with one.

entries.clue: Delayed being strict on parade ground (14)

indicators.note: the letters are ground up, pulverised

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 14 letters

annotation.surface: A soldier held up by a sergeant major's discipline on the drill square.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Parade ground' reads as one military phrase; 'ground' is split off as the past tense of grind.
annotation.definitionFit: To procrastinate is to delay or put off action.

entries.clue: Appear to cause embarrassment (4,2)

blocks.note: to arrive or turn up
to show someone up is to embarrass them

annotation.surface: Turning up just to embarrass someone.
annotation.walkthrough: Both senses are everyday phrasal verbs; the clue simply sets them side by side.
annotation.definitionFit: Show up means both to arrive and to embarrass someone in public.

entries.clue: Warning about depression, right? (3,5)

blocks.note: re = about, concerning
a dale is a valley, a depression in the land
RT = right

annotation.surface: A mental-health warning, seeking reassurance it is right.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Depression' suggests low mood or weather, but here it is a dip in the ground.
annotation.definitionFit: A red alert is the most urgent warning of danger.
